headline: High-risk workspace and MCP interaction: Roo Code can write/egress broadly while awesome-nlp is non-runnable and offers no isolation, creating default data-leak and conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read workspace files, run browsers, and use MCP; its shared state is via filesystem. awesome-nlp is an open-source list with no I/O surfaces, so direct injection into it is absent, but any shared workspace or MCP content could be treated as trusted by Roo Code. The pathway is plausible, not proven.
conditions: IF Roo Code is pointed at a workspace containing attacker-controlled files or MCP output, THEN prompt injection is possible.
IF an operator manually copies content from awesome-nlp into Roo Code, THEN injected instructions can be parsed.
mitigations: Disable MCP servers for the session.
Keep Roo Code in a dedicated empty workspace.
Review any file or browser content before pasting into Roo Code.
Use read-only copies for untrusted artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all external content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code touches source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider APIs, while awesome-nlp has no data classes or runtime surfaces. There is no direct evidence that awesome-nlp leaks data, but Roo Code can exfiltrate workspace contents through configured APIs or MCP. The pairwise risk is workspace-based and plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the VS Code workspace, THEN Roo Code can transmit them to configured model APIs or MCP servers.
IF browser screenshots contain secrets, THEN Roo Code may include them in prompts or outputs.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace.
Use a local-only model backend if available.
Disable MCP servers unless needed.
Restrict the workspace to non-sensitive files.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git-state modification, and shared state via filesystem across instances. awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no write surface, so it does not counterbalance the conflict. In a shared workspace, Roo Code instances can race and corrupt git or files by default.
conditions: IF two Roo Code instances operate in the same VS Code workspace, THEN file and git conflicts can occur.
IF the workspace is shared with other editors or agents, THEN last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Use one agent per workspace.
Pause other editors during agent runs.
Commit or stash before starting a session.
Work on a branch with frequent checkpoints.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on generated content through shell, git, and browser tools, so if it consumes outputs derived from awesome-nlp or copied from it, errors can cascade into actions. awesome-nlp itself is only a static list, so it is not an active verifier. The interaction exists, but the blast radius is usually bounded to the workspace.
conditions: IF Roo Code treats copied text from awesome-nlp as authoritative instructions, THEN it may execute incorrect actions.
IF Roo Code uses generated facts to edit files or commit code, THEN downstream errors can persist.
mitigations: Require human review before execution.
Separate research notes from executable instructions.
Use a checklist for any shell or git action.
Verify claims against primary sources.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before tool actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No sensitive regulated data class is documented for awesome-nlp, and Roo Code lists source code and browser screenshots only. There is no evidence of residency or certification mismatch in the pair, so compliance risk is limited to generic handling of workspace content. The other agent is not cited beyond its lack of regulated data surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the VS Code workspace, THEN Roo Code's outbound APIs may create a policy mismatch.
IF browser screenshots capture personal data, THEN retention policies must be checked.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace.
Review provider retention settings.
Disable screenshot capture when unnecessary.
Document data-handling expectations for the session.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
